audit_status.source_base: Hebrew 2 Samuel chapter 15, first-pass draft aligned later
audit_status.review_note: Reviewed for Absalom's image campaign, real judicial access failure, religious pretext, uninformed followers, David's flight, ten concubines left behind, foreign/exile troops and children, public grief, ark politics, priestly intelligence network, Hushai's dangerous assignment, and leader-centered valuation.

verses.restored: After this Absalom prepared for himself a chariot, horses, and fifty men running before him.

familiar.text: And it came to pass after this, that Absalom prepared him chariots and horses, and fifty men to run before him.

modern.text: Some time later, Absalom provided for himself a chariot with horses and fifty men to run ahead of him.

original.text: וַֽיְהִי֙ מֵאַ֣חֲרֵי כֵ֔ן וַיַּ֤עַשׂ לוֹ֙ אַבְשָׁל֔וֹם מֶרְכָּבָ֖ה וְסֻסִ֑ים וַחֲמִשִּׁ֥ים אִ֖ישׁ רָצִ֥ים לְפָנָֽיו

verses.restored: Absalom rose early and stood beside road of gate. Whenever any man with dispute came to king for judgment, Absalom called and said, From what city are you? He said, Your servant is from one of tribes of Israel.

familiar.text: And Absalom rose up early, and stood beside the way of the gate: and it was so, that when any man that had a controversy came to the king for judgment, then Absalom called unto him, and said, Of what city art thou? And he said, Thy servant is of one of the tribes of Israel.

modern.text: He would get up early and stand beside the road leading to the city gate. Whenever anyone had a grievance to bring before the king for a decision, Absalom would call out and ask, “What city are you from?” And if he replied, “Your servant is from one of the tribes of Israel,”

original.text: וְהִשְׁכִּים֙ אַבְשָׁל֔וֹם וְעָמַ֕ד עַל יַ֖ד דֶּ֣רֶךְ הַשָּׁ֑עַר וַיְהִ֡י כָּל הָאִ֣ישׁ אֲשֶֽׁר יִהְיֶה לּוֹ רִיב֩ לָב֨וֹא אֶל הַמֶּ֜לֶךְ לַמִּשְׁפָּ֗ט וַיִּקְרָ֨א אַבְשָׁל֤וֹם אֵלָיו֙ וַיֹּ֗אמֶר אֵֽי מִזֶּ֥ה עִיר֙ אַ֔תָּה וַיֹּ֕אמֶר מֵאַחַ֥ד שִׁבְטֵֽי יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל עַבְדֶּֽךָ

verses.restored: Absalom said to him, See, your matters are good and right, but there is no one appointed by king to hear you.

familiar.text: And Absalom said unto him, See, thy matters are good and right; but there is no man deputed of the king to hear thee.

modern.text: Absalom would say, “Look, your claims are good and right, but the king has no deputy to hear you.”

original.text: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר אֵלָיו֙ אַבְשָׁל֔וֹם רְאֵ֥ה דְבָרֶ֖ךָ טוֹבִ֣ים וּנְכֹחִ֑ים וְשֹׁמֵ֥עַ אֵין לְךָ֖ מֵאֵ֥ת הַמֶּֽלֶךְ

verses.restored: Absalom said, Who will appoint me judge in land, so every man with dispute or judgment may come to me and I will make him right?

familiar.text: Absalom said moreover, Oh that I were made judge in the land, that every man which hath any suit or cause might come unto me, and I would do him justice!

modern.text: And he would add, “If only someone would appoint me judge in the land, then everyone with a grievance or dispute could come to me, and I would give him justice.”

original.text: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר֙ אַבְשָׁל֔וֹם מִי יְשִׂמֵ֥נִי שֹׁפֵ֖ט בָּאָ֑רֶץ וְעָלַ֗י יָב֥וֹא כָּל אִ֛ישׁ אֲשֶֽׁר יִהְיֶה לּוֹ רִ֥יב וּמִשְׁפָּ֖ט וְהִצְדַּקְתִּֽיו

verses.restored: When a man came near to bow to him, he stretched out his hand, took hold of him, and kissed him.

familiar.text: And it was so, that when any man came nigh to him to do him obeisance, he put forth his hand, and took him, and kissed him.

modern.text: Also, when anyone approached to bow down to him, Absalom would reach out his hand, take hold of him, and kiss him.

original.text: וְהָיָה֙ בִּקְרָב אִ֔ישׁ לְהִשְׁתַּחֲוֺ֖ת ל֑וֹ וְשָׁלַ֧ח אֶת יָד֛וֹ וְהֶחֱזִ֥יק ל֖וֹ וְנָ֥שַׁק לֽוֹ

verses.restored: Absalom did according to this manner to all Israel who came to king for judgment. Absalom stole/turned hearts of men of Israel.

familiar.text: And on this manner did Absalom to all Israel that came to the king for judgment: so Absalom stole the hearts of the men of Israel.

modern.text: Absalom did this to all the Israelites who came to the king for justice. In this way he stole the hearts of the men of Israel.

original.text: וַיַּ֨עַשׂ אַבְשָׁל֜וֹם כַּדָּבָ֤ר הַזֶּה֙ לְכָל יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל אֲשֶׁר יָבֹ֥אוּ לַמִּשְׁפָּ֖ט אֶל הַמֶּ֑לֶךְ וַיְגַנֵּב֙ אַבְשָׁל֔וֹם אֶת לֵ֖ב אַנְשֵׁ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵֽל

verses.restored: At end of forty years/four years, Absalom said to king, Please let me go and complete my vow that I vowed to YHWH at Hebron.

familiar.text: And it came to pass after forty years, that Absalom said unto the king, I pray thee, let me go and pay my vow, which I have vowed unto the LORD, in Hebron.

modern.text: After four years had passed, Absalom said to the king, “Please let me go to Hebron to fulfill a vow I have made to the LORD.

original.text: וַיְהִ֕י מִקֵּ֖ץ אַרְבָּעִ֣ים שָׁנָ֑ה וַיֹּ֤אמֶר אַבְשָׁלוֹם֙ אֶל הַמֶּ֔לֶךְ אֵ֣לֲכָה נָּ֗א וַאֲשַׁלֵּ֛ם אֶת נִדְרִ֛י אֲשֶׁר נָדַ֥רְתִּי לַֽיהוָ֖ה בְּחֶבְרֽוֹן

verses.restored: Your servant vowed while I lived at Geshur in Aram, saying, If YHWH truly returns me to Jerusalem, I will serve YHWH.

familiar.text: For thy servant vowed a vow while I abode at Geshur in Syria, saying, If the LORD shall bring me again indeed to Jerusalem, then I will serve the LORD.

modern.text: For your servant made a vow while dwelling in Geshur of Aram, saying: ‘If indeed the LORD brings me back to Jerusalem, I will worship the LORD in Hebron.’ ”

original.text: כִּי נֵ֨דֶר֙ נָדַ֣ר עַבְדְּךָ֔ בְּשִׁבְתִּ֥י בִגְשׁ֛וּר בַּאֲרָ֖ם לֵאמֹ֑ר אִם ישיב יְשִׁיבֵ֤נִי יְהוָה֙ יְר֣וּשָׁלִַ֔ם וְעָבַדְתִּ֖י אֶת יְהוָֽה

verses.restored: King said to him, Go in peace. He arose and went to Hebron.

familiar.text: And the king said unto him, Go in peace. So he arose, and went to Hebron.

modern.text: “Go in peace,” said the king. So Absalom got up and went to Hebron.

original.text: וַיֹּֽאמֶר ל֥וֹ הַמֶּ֖לֶךְ לֵ֣ךְ בְּשָׁל֑וֹם וַיָּ֖קָם וַיֵּ֥לֶךְ חֶבְרֽוֹנָה

verses.restored: Absalom sent spies throughout all tribes of Israel, saying, When you hear sound of shofar, say, Absalom reigns at Hebron.

familiar.text: But Absalom sent spies throughout all the tribes of Israel, saying, As soon as ye hear the sound of the trumpet, then ye shall say, Absalom reigneth in Hebron.

modern.text: Then Absalom sent spies throughout the tribes of Israel with this message: “When you hear the sound of the horn, you are to say, ‘Absalom reigns in Hebron!’”

original.text: וַיִּשְׁלַ֤ח אַבְשָׁלוֹם֙ מְרַגְּלִ֔ים בְּכָל שִׁבְטֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל לֵאמֹ֑ר כְּשָׁמְעֲכֶם֙ אֶת ק֣וֹל הַשֹּׁפָ֔ר וַאֲמַרְתֶּ֕ם מָלַ֥ךְ אַבְשָׁל֖וֹם בְּחֶבְרֽוֹן

verses.restored: With Absalom went two hundred men from Jerusalem who were called. They went in their innocence and did not know anything.

familiar.text: And with Absalom went two hundred men out of Jerusalem, that were called; and they went in their simplicity, and they knew not any thing.

modern.text: Two hundred men from Jerusalem accompanied Absalom. They had been invited as guests and they went along innocently, for they knew nothing about the matter.

original.text: וְאֶת אַבְשָׁל֗וֹם הָלְכ֞וּ מָאתַ֤יִם אִישׁ֙ מִיר֣וּשָׁלִַ֔ם קְרֻאִ֖ים וְהֹלְכִ֣ים לְתֻמָּ֑ם וְלֹ֥א יָדְע֖וּ כָּל דָּבָֽר

verses.restored: Absalom sent for Ahithophel the Gilonite, counselor of David, from his city Giloh, while he offered sacrifices. Conspiracy became strong, and people with Absalom continually increased.

familiar.text: And Absalom sent for Ahithophel the Gilonite, David’s counsellor, from his city, even from Giloh, while he offered sacrifices. And the conspiracy was strong; for the people increased continually with Absalom.

modern.text: While Absalom was offering the sacrifices, he sent for Ahithophel the Gilonite, David’s counselor, to come from his hometown of Giloh. So the conspiracy gained strength, and Absalom’s following kept increasing. David Flees Jerusalem (Psalms 3:1–8)

original.text: וַיִּשְׁלַ֣ח אַ֠בְשָׁלוֹם אֶת אֲחִיתֹ֨פֶל הַגִּֽילֹנִ֜י יוֹעֵ֣ץ דָּוִ֗ד מֵֽעִירוֹ֙ מִגִּלֹ֔ה בְּזָבְח֖וֹ אֶת הַזְּבָחִ֑ים וַיְהִ֤י הַקֶּ֨שֶׁר֙ אַמִּ֔ץ וְהָעָ֛ם הוֹלֵ֥ךְ וָרָ֖ב אֶת אַבְשָׁלֽוֹם

verses.restored: Messenger came to David, saying, Heart of men of Israel is after Absalom.

familiar.text: And there came a messenger to David, saying, The hearts of the men of Israel are after Absalom.

modern.text: Then a messenger came to David and reported, “The hearts of the men of Israel are with Absalom.”

original.text: וַיָּבֹא֙ הַמַּגִּ֔יד אֶל דָּוִ֖ד לֵאמֹ֑ר הָיָ֛ה לֶב אִ֥ישׁ יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל אַחֲרֵ֥י אַבְשָׁלֽוֹם

verses.restored: David said to all his servants with him in Jerusalem, Arise and let us flee, because there will be no escape for us from face of Absalom. Hurry to go, lest he quickly overtake us, drive evil upon us, and strike city by edge of sword.

familiar.text: And David said unto all his servants that were with him at Jerusalem, Arise, and let us flee; for we shall not else escape from Absalom: make speed to depart, lest he overtake us suddenly, and bring evil upon us, and smite the city with the edge of the sword.

modern.text: And David said to all the servants with him in Jerusalem, “Arise and let us flee, or we will not escape from Absalom! We must leave quickly, or he will soon overtake us, heap disaster on us, and put the city to the sword.”

original.text: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר דָּ֠וִד לְכָל עֲבָדָ֨יו אֲשֶׁר אִתּ֤וֹ בִירוּשָׁלִַ֨ם֙ ק֣וּמוּ וְנִבְרָ֔חָה כִּ֛י לֹא תִֽהְיֶה לָּ֥נוּ פְלֵיטָ֖ה מִפְּנֵ֣י אַבְשָׁל֑וֹם מַהֲר֣וּ לָלֶ֗כֶת פֶּן יְמַהֵ֤ר וְהִשִּׂגָ֨נוּ֙ וְהִדִּ֤יחַ עָלֵ֨ינוּ֙ אֶת הָ֣רָעָ֔ה וְהִכָּ֥ה הָעִ֖יר לְפִי חָֽרֶב

verses.restored: Servants of king said to king, According to all my lord king chooses, look, your servants.

familiar.text: And the king’s servants said unto the king, Behold, thy servants are ready to do whatsoever my lord the king shall appoint.

modern.text: The king’s servants replied, “Whatever our lord the king decides, we are your servants.”

original.text: וַיֹּאמְר֥וּ עַבְדֵֽי הַמֶּ֖לֶךְ אֶל הַמֶּ֑לֶךְ כְּכֹ֧ל אֲשֶׁר יִבְחַ֛ר אֲדֹנִ֥י הַמֶּ֖לֶךְ הִנֵּ֥ה עֲבָדֶֽיךָ

verses.restored: King went out, and all his household at his feet. King left ten women, concubines, to guard house.

familiar.text: And the king went forth, and all his household after him. And the king left ten women, which were concubines, to keep the house.

modern.text: Then the king set out, and his entire household followed him. But he left behind ten concubines to take care of the palace.

original.text: וַיֵּצֵ֥א הַמֶּ֛לֶךְ וְכָל בֵּית֖וֹ בְּרַגְלָ֑יו וַיַּעֲזֹ֣ב הַמֶּ֗לֶךְ אֵ֣ת עֶ֧שֶׂר נָשִׁ֛ים פִּֽלַגְשִׁ֖ים לִשְׁמֹ֥ר הַבָּֽיִת

verses.restored: King went out and all people at his feet, and they stood at last house/place far off.

familiar.text: And the king went forth, and all the people after him, and tarried in a place that was far off.

modern.text: So the king set out with all the people following him. He stopped at the last house,

original.text: וַיֵּצֵ֥א הַמֶּ֛לֶךְ וְכָל הָעָ֖ם בְּרַגְלָ֑יו וַיַּעַמְד֖וּ בֵּ֥ית הַמֶּרְחָֽק

verses.restored: All his servants crossed beside him: all Cherethites, all Pelethites, and all Gittites, six hundred men who came at his feet from Gath, crossed before king.

familiar.text: And all his servants passed on beside him; and all the Cherethites, and all the Pelethites, and all the Gittites, six hundred men which came after him from Gath, passed on before the king.

modern.text: and all his servants marched past him—all the Cherethites and Pelethites, and six hundred Gittites who had followed him from Gath.

original.text: וְכָל עֲבָדָיו֙ עֹבְרִ֣ים עַל יָד֔וֹ וְכָל הַכְּרֵתִ֖י וְכָל הַפְּלֵתִ֑י וְכָֽל הַגִּתִּ֞ים שֵׁשׁ מֵא֣וֹת אִ֗ישׁ אֲשֶׁר בָּ֤אוּ בְרַגְלוֹ֙ מִגַּ֔ת עֹבְרִ֖ים עַל פְּנֵ֥י הַמֶּֽלֶךְ

verses.restored: King said to Ittai the Gittite, Why do you also go with us? Return and stay with king, because you are a foreigner and also an exile from your place.

familiar.text: Then said the king to Ittai the Gittite, Wherefore goest thou also with us? return to thy place, and abide with the king: for thou art a stranger, and also an exile.

modern.text: Then the king said to Ittai the Gittite, “Why should you also go with us? Go back and stay with the new king, since you are both a foreigner and an exile from your homeland.

original.text: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר הַמֶּ֨לֶךְ֙ אֶל אִתַּ֣י הַגִּתִּ֔י לָ֧מָּה תֵלֵ֛ךְ גַּם אַתָּ֖ה אִתָּ֑נוּ שׁ֣וּב וְשֵׁ֤ב עִם הַמֶּ֨לֶךְ֙ כִּֽי נָכְרִ֣י אַ֔תָּה וְגַם גֹּלֶ֥ה אַתָּ֖ה לִמְקוֹמֶֽךָ

verses.restored: You came yesterday; shall I make you wander with us today while I go wherever I go? Return and return your brothers with you. Covenant-kindness and faithfulness be with you.

familiar.text: Whereas thou camest but yesterday, should I this day make thee go up and down with us? seeing I go whither I may, return thou, and take back thy brethren: mercy and truth be with thee.

modern.text: In fact, you arrived only yesterday; should I make you wander around with us today while I do not know where I am going? Go back and take your brothers with you. May the LORD show you loving devotion and faithfulness. ”

original.text: תְּמ֣וֹל בּוֹאֶ֗ךָ וְהַיּ֞וֹם אנועך עִמָּ֨נוּ֙ לָלֶ֔כֶת וַאֲנִ֣י הוֹלֵ֔ךְ עַ֥ל אֲשֶׁר אֲנִ֖י הוֹלֵ֑ךְ שׁ֣וּב וְהָשֵׁ֧ב אֶת אַחֶ֛יךָ עִמָּ֖ךְ חֶ֥סֶד וֶאֱמֶֽת

verses.restored: Ittai answered king and said, As YHWH lives and as my lord king lives, in place where my lord king is, whether for death or life, there your servant will be.

familiar.text: And Ittai answered the king, and said, As the LORD liveth, and as my lord the king liveth, surely in what place my lord the king shall be, whether in death or life, even there also will thy servant be.

modern.text: But Ittai answered the king, “As surely as the LORD lives, and as my lord the king lives, wherever my lord the king may be, whether it means life or death, there will your servant be!”

original.text: וַיַּ֧עַן אִתַּ֛י אֶת הַמֶּ֖לֶךְ וַיֹּאמַ֑ר חַי יְהוָ֗ה וְחֵי֙ אֲדֹנִ֣י הַמֶּ֔לֶךְ כִּ֠י אִם בִּמְק֞וֹם אֲשֶׁ֥ר יִֽהְיֶה שָּׁ֣ם אֲדֹנִ֣י הַמֶּ֗לֶךְ אִם לְמָ֨וֶת֙ אִם לְחַיִּ֔ים כִּי שָׁ֖ם יִהְיֶ֥ה עַבְדֶּֽךָ

verses.restored: David said to Ittai, Go and cross. Ittai the Gittite crossed, and all his men and all little ones who were with him.

familiar.text: And David said to Ittai, Go and pass over. And Ittai the Gittite passed over, and all his men, and all the little ones that were with him.

modern.text: “March on then,” said David to Ittai. So Ittai the Gittite marched past with all his men and all the little ones who were with him.

original.text: וַיֹּ֧אמֶר דָּוִ֛ד אֶל אִתַּ֖י לֵ֣ךְ וַעֲבֹ֑ר וַֽיַּעֲבֹ֞ר אִתַּ֤י הַגִּתִּי֙ וְכָל אֲנָשָׁ֔יו וְכָל הַטַּ֖ף אֲשֶׁ֥ר אִתּֽוֹ

verses.restored: All land wept with a great voice. All people crossed, and king crossed wadi Kidron. All people crossed toward way of wilderness.

familiar.text: And all the country wept with a loud voice, and all the people passed over: the king also himself passed over the brook Kidron, and all the people passed over, toward the way of the wilderness.

modern.text: Everyone in the countryside was weeping loudly as all the people passed by. And as the king crossed the Kidron Valley, all the people also passed toward the way of the wilderness.

original.text: וְכָל הָאָ֗רֶץ בּוֹכִים֙ ק֣וֹל גָּד֔וֹל וְכָל הָעָ֖ם עֹֽבְרִ֑ים וְהַמֶּ֗לֶךְ עֹבֵר֙ בְּנַ֣חַל קִדְר֔וֹן וְכָל הָעָם֙ עֹבְרִ֔ים עַל פְּנֵי דֶ֖רֶךְ אֶת הַמִּדְבָּֽר

verses.restored: Look, Zadok also and all Levites with him carried ark of covenant of Divine. They set down ark of Divine, and Abiathar went up until all people finished crossing from city.

familiar.text: And lo Zadok also, and all the Levites were with him, bearing the ark of the covenant of God: and they set down the ark of God; and Abiathar went up, until all the people had done passing out of the city.

modern.text: Zadok was also there, and all the Levites with him were carrying the ark of the covenant of God. And they set down the ark of God, and Abiathar offered sacrifices until the people had passed out of the city.

original.text: וְהִנֵּ֨ה גַם צָד֜וֹק וְכָֽל הַלְוִיִּ֣ם אִתּ֗וֹ נֹֽשְׂאִים֙ אֶת אֲרוֹן֙ בְּרִ֣ית הָאֱלֹהִ֔ים וַיַּצִּ֨קוּ֙ אֶת אֲר֣וֹן הָאֱלֹהִ֔ים וַיַּ֖עַל אֶבְיָתָ֑ר עַד תֹּ֥ם כָּל הָעָ֖ם לַעֲב֥וֹר מִן הָעִֽיר

verses.restored: King said to Zadok, Return ark of Divine to city. If I find favor in eyes of YHWH, YHWH will return me and show me it and its dwelling.

familiar.text: And the king said unto Zadok, Carry back the ark of God into the city: if I shall find favour in the eyes of the LORD, he will bring me again, and shew me both it, and his habitation:

modern.text: Then the king said to Zadok, “Return the ark of God to the city. If I find favor in the eyes of the LORD, He will bring me back and let me see both it and His dwelling place again.

original.text: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר הַמֶּ֨לֶךְ֙ לְצָד֔וֹק הָשֵׁ֛ב אֶת אֲר֥וֹן הָאֱלֹהִ֖ים הָעִ֑יר אִם אֶמְצָ֥א חֵן֙ בְּעֵינֵ֣י יְהוָ֔ה וֶהֱשִׁבַ֕נִי וְהִרְאַ֥נִי אֹת֖וֹ וְאֶת נָוֵֽהוּ

verses.restored: If YHWH says thus, I have no delight in you, look, here I am; let YHWH do to me what is good in YHWH's eyes.

familiar.text: But if he thus say, I have no delight in thee; behold, here am I, let him do to me as seemeth good unto him.

modern.text: But if He should say, ‘I do not delight in you,’ then here I am; let Him do to me whatever seems good to Him.”

original.text: וְאִם֙ כֹּ֣ה יֹאמַ֔ר לֹ֥א חָפַ֖צְתִּי בָּ֑ךְ הִנְנִ֕י יַֽעֲשֶׂה לִּ֕י כַּאֲשֶׁ֥ר ט֖וֹב בְּעֵינָֽיו

verses.restored: King said to Zadok the priest, Are you not a seer? Return to city in peace, and your two sons with you: Ahimaaz your son and Jonathan son of Abiathar.

familiar.text: The king said also unto Zadok the priest, Art not thou a seer? return into the city in peace, and your two sons with you, Ahimaaz thy son, and Jonathan the son of Abiathar.

modern.text: The king also said to Zadok the priest, “Are you not a seer? Return to the city in peace—you with your son Ahimaaz, and Abiathar with his son Jonathan.

verses.restored: See, I will wait at crossings/plains of wilderness until word comes from you to report to me.

familiar.text: See, I will tarry in the plain of the wilderness, until there come word from you to certify me.

modern.text: See, I will wait at the fords of the wilderness until word comes from you to inform me.”

original.text: רְאוּ֙ אָנֹכִ֣י מִתְמַהְמֵ֔הַּ בעברות הַמִּדְבָּ֑ר עַ֣ד בּ֥וֹא דָבָ֛ר מֵעִמָּכֶ֖ם לְהַגִּ֥יד לִֽי

familiar.text: Zadok therefore and Abiathar carried the ark of God again to Jerusalem: and they tarried there.

modern.text: So Zadok and Abiathar returned the ark of God to Jerusalem and stayed there. David Weeps at the Mount of Olives (Psalms 63:1–11)

original.text: וַיָּ֨שֶׁב צָד֧וֹק וְאֶבְיָתָ֛ר אֶת אֲר֥וֹן הָאֱלֹהִ֖ים יְרוּשָׁלִָ֑ם וַיֵּשְׁב֖וּ שָֽׁם

verses.restored: David went up ascent of Olives, going and weeping, his head covered, walking barefoot. All people with him covered each his head, going up and weeping.

familiar.text: And David went up by the ascent of mount Olivet, and wept as he went up, and had his head covered, and he went barefoot: and all the people that was with him covered every man his head, and they went up, weeping as they went up.

modern.text: But David continued up the Mount of Olives, weeping as he went up. His head was covered, and he was walking barefoot. And all the people with him covered their heads and went up, weeping as they went.

familiar.text: And one told David, saying, Ahithophel is among the conspirators with Absalom. And David said, O LORD, I pray thee, turn the counsel of Ahithophel into foolishness.

modern.text: Now someone told David: “Ahithophel is among the conspirators with Absalom.” So David pleaded, “O LORD, please turn the counsel of Ahithophel into foolishness!”

familiar.text: And it came to pass, that when David was come to the top of the mount, where he worshipped God, behold, Hushai the Archite came to meet him with his coat rent, and earth upon his head:

modern.text: When David came to the summit, where he used to worship God, Hushai the Archite was there to meet him with his robe torn and dust on his head.

familiar.text: Unto whom David said, If thou passest on with me, then thou shalt be a burden unto me:

modern.text: David said to him, “If you go on with me, you will be a burden to me.

modern.text: But you can thwart the counsel of Ahithophel for me if you return to the city and say to Absalom: ‘I will be your servant, my king; in the past I was your father’s servant, but now I will be your servant.’

modern.text: Will not Zadok and Abiathar the priests be there with you? Report to them everything you hear from the king’s palace.

familiar.text: Behold, they have there with them their two sons, Ahimaaz Zadok’s son, and Jonathan Abiathar’s son; and by them ye shall send unto me every thing that ye can hear.

modern.text: Indeed, their two sons, Ahimaaz son of Zadok and Jonathan son of Abiathar, are there with them. Send them to me with everything you hear.”

original.text: וַיָּבֹ֥א חוּשַׁ֛י רֵעֶ֥ה דָוִ֖ד הָעִ֑יר וְאַבְשָׁלֹ֔ם יָבֹ֖א יְרוּשָׁלִָֽם

translation_notes: Absalom exploits a genuine governance failure: petitioners cannot access a royal judge. Charismatic manipulation and legitimate grievance can coexist.
Physical pageantry, kisses, and promises of universal justice build a personality-centered campaign. Appearance of closeness is not accountable public service.
The 'forty years' reading is chronologically difficult; many witnesses/readings support four years. The number must remain flagged.
Two hundred invited men do not know the conspiracy. Presence in a political crowd does not establish informed consent or guilt.
David leaves ten concubines to guard the palace. They are exposed to predictable danger without recorded consent and later become targets of political sexual violence.
Ittai is a Gittite, foreigner, and exile. David gives him an exit, but his soldiers and 'little ones' still enter a dangerous civil-war migration.
The ark is sent back rather than used as a royal talisman. Yet Zadok, Abiathar, and their sons become an intelligence network, placing religious workers and young messengers at risk.
David calls Hushai a burden because of tactical need; age, disability, distress, or reduced mobility must not make a person inherently burdensome.
The chapter's weeping includes a whole displaced population, not merely a fallen ruler.
safety_note: Do not romanticize political charm, weaponize religious vows, blame uninformed followers, or make refugees prove loyalty through danger. Center the ten women abandoned in the palace, children crossing into exile, ordinary petitioners denied justice, and people turned into intelligence assets by competing rulers.
